 Shelly Palmer: Are you investing in a feature?
 Think About This: OpenAI says its offering makes decisions up to 10 times faster than using the same underlying model through its general-purpose service. 
Shelly Palmer Oct 23, 2026 9:03 AM 
 Share by Email 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Share on LinkedIn 
 Print 
 Share via Text Message 
 shellypalmer.com 
 Listen to this article 
 00:02:50 
 Greetings from New York. Within 24 hours of its debut on September 15, TypeSafe's Jev , an AI model that helps developers get faster, cheaper results when using LLMs, became the fastest-adopted model in Vercel's AI Gateway history. Within a few weeks, there were knock-offs all over GitHub.
 Yesterday, OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available. It's a direct Jev competitor that lets software make quick choices, such as classifying a document, routing a customer request, or choosing the next action in an automated workflow.
 OpenAI says its offering makes decisions up to 10 times faster than using the same underlying model through its general-purpose service. That comparison is with OpenAI’s own product. Customers quoted in the announcement include Box, Datadog, Ramp, Sierra, and Speak. Speak says its testing reduced the time to the next action in its language-learning application from 1.4 seconds to 0.13 seconds.
 OpenAI charges $0.10 per million input tokens, with no output-token charge. Cached input has separate pricing. The service supports text and images, with regional processing available in the United States and European Union.
 For years, one of the most important questions for any new product or service has been, "Are you creating a feature or creating a business?" If you don't have a clear answer to that question, and you invest in an AI startup (or any startup for that matter), you are bearish on AGI.
 As always, your thoughts and comments are both welcome and encouraged. -s
 P.S. Yesterday, I focused on a PHP bug that highlighted some of the dangers of AI-enhanced cybersecurity. I've been following the news closely. Several websites have been temporarily taken out of service as a precaution while patches were applied. Researchers have reported widespread exploitation attempts , but so far there have been no reports of this particular vulnerability being exploited in any significant way.
 About Shelly Palmer
 Shelly Palmer is the Professor of Advanced Media in Residence at Syracuse University’s S.I. Newhouse School of Public Communications and CEO of The Palmer Group, a consulting practice that helps Fortune 500 companies with technology, media and marketing. Named  LinkedIn’s “Top Voice in Technology,”  he covers tech and business for  Good Day New York , is a regular commentator on CNN and writes a popular  daily business blog .
